archetypes.name: shell-parity
archetypes.rationale: The plan ports eight shell scripts with subtle exit/status and git-state behavior where mismatches would invalidate the phase.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the planned Python surfaces against the named shell scripts and identify places where the plan omits observable shell behavior, exit semantics, environment variables, dirty-tree rules, or command sequencing. Pay special attention to logic split between standalone scripts and embedded ship-pr.sh bump-phase behavior, since the plan claims parity across both. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: changelog-schema
archetypes.rationale: Markdown/RST changelog editing and conflict resolution are contract-heavy and easy to underspecify across docs, tests, and shell parity.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect whether the changelog portion of the plan fully matches repo evidence for heading formats, section anchors, duplicate handling, conflict-stage reads, and commit/drop contracts. Look for schema drift between Markdown and RST handling, especially where RST support is net-new rather than bash-parity. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: cutover-boundary
archetypes.rationale: This phase must stay additive and unwired until Phase 7, so accidental runtime coupling or missing boundary checks are plan-level risks.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the plan for violations of the strangler-fig boundary: imports from live skill paths, deletion or replacement of shell scripts, runtime dependency creep, or changes that would affect /implement before Phase 7. Also check whether the scoped files are sufficient for constants, git helpers, docs, and tests without touching runtime surfaces outside the stated additive Python tree. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
